title: Multiplication and product comparison descend from strict quotient cones
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $R$, a uniformizer $\varpi$ and $A_n=R/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For each scheme $W$ under consideration assume $\ell$ invertible on $W$, use its small pro-etale site in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], and put $B_{W,n}=(A_n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $c_n:g^{-1}B_{Y,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{X,n}$ and $c:g^{-1}\widehat R_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat R_X$ be the coefficient structure maps, with $\pi_{X,n}c=c_n g^{-1}(\pi_{Y,n})$, and let $G$ be termwise inverse image with completed scalars transported through $c$ [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image, def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. For $N\in D(\widehat R_Y)$ choose any flat-term K-flat representative $q:Q\to N$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Put $Q_n=Q\otimes_{\widehat R_Y}B_{Y,n}$, with quotient transitions $\tau_n$, $D=U_Y(Q_n)_n$, and $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_n g_n^*Q_n$, with the actual strict pullback quotient transitions [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Here $g_n^*M=g^{-1}M\otimes_{g^{-1}B_{Y,n}}B_{X,n}$ uses the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

The functor $G$ is additive and exact and its canonical countable-product comparison $\phi_D:G(\prod_n D_n)\to\prod_n GD_n$, characterized by the projections, is an isomorphism. Multiplication
$$j_n:C_n\longrightarrow GD_n,\qquad x\otimes a\longmapsto ax$$
is $\widehat R_X$-linear, with inverse $i_n:x\mapsto x\otimes1$. These are inverse isomorphisms of strict tower complexes $j:C\xrightarrow{\sim}GD$: they commute with restrictions, differentials and quotient transitions, and are natural in chain maps between representatives $Q$.

Put $H(Z)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Z)[-1]$, with $s_Z((z_n))=(t_nz_{n+1})$ and differential $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_Z)a,da)$ on $(\prod Z_n^{i-1})\oplus(\prod Z_n^i)$. Through the normalized strict Roos identifications [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], the canonical exact-product derived-limit comparison [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-strict-limit] is an isomorphism
$$\eta_D:GH(D)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(GD)$$
whose maps on the two product coordinates are $\phi_D$, with no off-diagonal entry, and $\phi_DG(1-s_D)=(1-s_{GD})\phi_D$. Thus the isomorphism of complexes
$$\Theta_Q=\eta_D^{-1}H(j):H(C)\xrightarrow{\sim}GH(D)$$
descends to a natural isomorphism $\Theta_{g,N}:P_gN\xrightarrow{\sim}G(\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YN)$, where $P_g$ is the ambient completed pullback [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. It is independent of the choice of $Q$ under the canonical resolution comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. For every derived morphism $f:N\to N'$ one has
$$\Theta_{g,N'}P_g(f)=G(\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_Y(f))\Theta_{g,N}.$$
All coordinate descriptions concern entire strict quotient cones; no completeness, constructibility or boundedness assumption on $N$ is made.
